mechanism_claims.claim_text: Polydim-I has direct morphological evidence of mycobacterial cell-envelope/cell-wall disruption in SEM after peptide exposure.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: Polydim-I against M. abscessus subsp. massiliense GO 06
mechanism_claims.limitations: SEM supports cell-envelope/cell-wall disruption morphology but is not a molecular target-binding assay; primary text and Figure 2 caption differ on exact concentration labels, so no precise dose-response is inferred.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Polydim-I reduces intracellular bacterial burden in infected macrophage cultures, supporting phenotypic antimycobacterial activity in a host-cell infection context.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: Polydim-I against M. abscessus subsp. massiliense isolates/reference strains in BALB/c peritoneal macrophages
mechanism_claims.limitations: This is phenotypic CFU evidence and does not by itself prove macrophage activation or a direct molecular target.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: The article proposes cell envelope/cell wall damage as the likely activity context and separately hypothesizes possible macrophage potentiation; these are retained as limited interpretation rather than direct molecular mechanism.
mechanism_claims.limitations: Discussion-level macrophage activation is a hypothesis and is not upgraded to direct mechanism without a dedicated activation assay.

caution_findings.evidence_context: SEM and CFU assays support cell-envelope damage/phenotypic activity context; no receptor, enzyme, or binding target is established.
Discussion hypothesis that Polydim-I might potentiate macrophage clearance is not promoted to direct mechanism.
